newsitem.title: CHINA: China floods kill 41 in southern province.
newsitem.headline: China floods kill 41 in southern province.

text.p: Some of the worst floods in 20 years in China's southern Guangdong province have killed 41 people and affected 3.26 million residents, officials said on Thursday.
The floods along the Pearl River in the southern province bordering Hong Kong were among the worst for 20 years, state media have said.
At least 41 people were reported dead by Thursday and tens of thousands left homeless, an official of the provincial flood control headquarters said.

Officials estimated about 54,420 buildings had been destroyed by the floods, spawned by several days of torrential rain across southern China. Direct damage was estimated at 1.836 billion yuan ($221.2 million), the official said.
The worst-hit town was Qingyuan, where almost all roads were damaged and the old section of the city was under water, he said.

Passenger trains along China's premier railway line between Beijing and the Hong Kong district of Kowloon had been disrupted from Tuesday because of flooding along the stretch of track between the provincial capital, Guangzhou, and the town of Shaotou, an official of the Guangzhou Railway Company said.
Railway officials in Beijing said services had since resumed with trains re-routed along other tracks.
Floods strike large swathes of central and southern China each year, often killing hundreds, and sometimes thousands, of people and destroying large areas of crops.
